title: GPU signal fingerprinting ops checklist and investigation notes
content:
Purpose

Quick, practical playbook + working notes for capturing a reproducible "signal fingerprint" when we see short bursts of ECC/peer-link errors followed by a kernel/driver instability. Goal is to collect high-fidelity evidence we can correlate to PSU / backplane / ambient noise and to provide an ops checklist the next oncall can run without needing a lab tech.

Context / why different

We keep seeing short, high-frequency ECC bursts that do not always correlate with obvious thermal events. Previous writeups focused on resets, nvlink handshakes, and ECC counts. This doc tries a complementary tack: treat each burst as a waveform we can fingerprint (time-of-day, PSU telemetry, ambient rack sensor, powerline harmonic activity, link retrain time) and build minimal capture requirements so postmortem can match patterns across nodes.

Incident summary (example trace)

- Symptom: job fragmentally fails with CUDA context loss + driver crash; node evicted after watchdog reset.
- Observed telemetry: short ECC correctable error burst on GPU0 (3s window; ~70 CE spikes), followed by NVLink link retrain on GPU0-1, then kernel oops on nvidia driver and all pods on node restarted.
- Approx time: 2029-09-12 04:17 UTC
- Affected capacity: 1/24 nodes in rack-17; same server had similar intermittent spike 3 weeks prior.

Immediate oncall checklist (run this first)

1) Quarantine node from scheduler (K8s): cordon + drain with graceful 120s, if workload supports. If immediate eviction needed, force drain. Record drain time.

   - kubectl cordon <node>
   - kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120

2) Snapshot kernel logs & driver state (copy to safe location):
   - sudo journalctl -k --since "-15m" > /var/tmp/gpu-oom-journal-$(date -u +%s).log
   - sudo dmesg -T > /var/tmp/gpu-dmesg-$(date -u +%s).log
   - nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,ERROR,PCIE,POWER > /var/tmp/nvidia-q-$(date -u +%s).txt

3) Capture high-resolution telemetry (if available) for the +/-5m window:
   - Pull GPU ECC time-series (internal metrics): promql: rate(gpu_ecc_correctable_total[1m]) grouped by instance, gpu
   - Pull nvlink/pcie error counters: promql: increase(gpu_pcie_correctable_errors_total[5m])
   - Pull rack-level PDUs and PSU telemetry: prtg/power-api query for rack-17 last 30m (voltage/current/THD if available)

4) If node is reachable by console/ipmi, snapshot sensor logs (BMC) and attempt a soft power-cycle only after captures:
   - ipmitool sel elist | tail -n 50 > /var/tmp/bmc-sel-$(date -u +%s).log
   - ipmitool sensor list > /var/tmp/bmc-sensor-$(date -u +%s).log

5) If the cluster has our in-rack oscilloscope or scope patch-points, schedule a 1hr capture with the lab (see experiments below). If not, escalate to hardware team with the fingerprint packet (below).

Fingerprint capture minimums (what we need to match patterns)

- GPU counters: per-GPU per-second ECC correctable counts, NVLink retrain counters, PCIe AER correctable counts. Resolution: 1s or better for first 30s around event.
- System sensors: PSU input voltage, PSU output voltage rails, 10Hz sampling or better for 2m window.
- BMC/PMIC counters: thermal, fan speeds, error logs (SEL).
- Rack-level metrics: PDU per-outlet current and voltage; ambient rack temp; total rack load.
- Time sync: ensure all captures have NTP-synced timestamps and include timezone/UTC marker.

Quick correlation checklist (what to look for)

- Does the ECC burst align with a short dip in PSU input (voltage sag) or a spike in current draw?
- Does NVLink retrain occur immediately after ECC peak (within 1–3s)? If yes, prefer link handshake hypotheses.
- Are there patterns across GPUs on the same PCIe root complex? If multi-GPU correlated, suspect backplane or slot power path.
- Any BMC SEL entries with PMIC/VR alerts within the same minute?
- Is the host kernel showing watchdog timeout or driver OOPS that references module symbols from nvidia.ko?

Diagnostic commands & quick artifacts to collect (ops friendly)

- nvidia-smi topo -m (topology snapshot)
- nvidia-smi -i 0 -q -d ECC,DISPLAY,ACCOUNTING > /tmp/gpu0-ecc.txt
- nvidia-smi nvlink -s (list nvlink status where supported)
- lspci -vvv -s <GPU-pci-slot> (check AER status)
- dmesg | egrep -i "gpu|nvidia|nvlink|aer|pci" > /tmp/dmesg-gpu.txt
- tcptrace/pcap: if workload was communicating with remote model store, capture relevant interface for 5m window (to rule out network-induced load spikes).

Hypotheses (short list, rough rank)

1) Micro-power transient on PSU input causing transient memory subsystem errors -> ECC bursts -> link retrain -> driver instability. (high plausibility if PDU shows dip)
2) Backplane connector marginal contact on NVLink lane leading to frequent retrain attempts under certain NVLink traffic patterns. (plausible if retrain counts high and only link-specific GPUs affected)
3) Driver kernel race triggered by repeated fast NVLink retrains (software-only) amplified by a particular driver revision. (plausible if many nodes show same driver stacktrace)
4) External RFI/noise in rack causing signal integrity glitches on mezzanine/backplane. (low by default but considered if lab captures show high-frequency noise)

Repro plan / experiments (lab team)

- Short reproducibility checklist for lab:
  1) Re-run known workload with deterministic memory access pattern (synthetic memtest + sustained nvlink traffic) and record ECC counters at 100ms resolution.
  2) Inject controlled PSU sag using programmable PDU to try to reproduce ECC bursts. Start with 5% voltage sag for 1s windows.
  3) Swap cable/backplane connectors between adjacent nodes to test transfer of failure.
  4) Roll driver to previous known-good revision (note exact package hash) and repeat.
  5) If possible, add a scope probe to NVLink differential pair pre/post retimer and look for common-mode spikes.

Temporary mitigations for production while we debug

- Prefer scheduled maintenance: cordon affected nodes and live-migrate critical customer jobs.
- If a node must stay in pool, set node-level eviction policy to lower max_concurrent_jobs and enable heartbeat timeouts to reduce sustained NVLink stress.
- Driver workaround: pin to older driver if lab shows clear improvement and a safe rollback exists.

Known unknowns / TODOs (short list)

- TODO: wire up 1s-resolution ECC counters into our short-history metrics index (owner: Arjun Patel) — ticket created: SRE-1124.
- TODO: test PDU programmable-sag experiment and capture waveform (owner: Sofia Mendes).
- TODO: build runbook snippet for oncall to request scope capture with lab (owner: Dylan Roe).
- Question: how often do we see this pattern across clusters in other regions? Quick query suggested ~6 similar events in last 90d but only 2 with matching NVLink retrain signature — need deeper matching.

Action items (owners and rough ETA)

- Arjun: instrument 1s ECC push for staging cluster, ETA 2029-09-28.
- Sofia: schedule lab window and run initial PSU sag tests, ETA 2029-10-04.
- Dylan: draft a short oncall playbook page and Slack shortcut for capture requests, ETA 2029-09-25.
- Leah: compile fingerprint examples from past 6 incidents into a short digest for hardware team, ETA 2029-09-22.

Notes to self / rough thoughts

- Keep this doc lean — the goal is to reduce friction for the next person oncall. Put deeper analysis into the confluence experiments page.
- If we can prove reproducibility with a 1s sag, we can likely work with datacenter ops to add input-side surge suppression or move node to redundant PSU bank.

Slack snippets to use (copy/paste)

- "SRE: node <node> experienced short ECC burst + nvlink retrain at <UTC>. We need 1s-resolution ECC and PSU readings for +/-5m. Please cordon and capture journal + nvidia-smi output. Escalate to hardware lab for scope capture if available. JIRA: SRE-1124"

Appendix: example promql snippets

- ecc rate per gpu (1s approximate): increase(gpu_ecc_correctable_total[1s])
- nvlink retrain count (5m window): increase(gpu_nvlink_retrains_total[5m])
- pdu voltage sag detection: increase(pdu_voltage_dips_total{rack="rack-17"}[5m])

End.
